a.x: When Aiman's family opened a homestay in their village near Kuala Kangsar, they were not sure anyone would come. Within six months, however, the homestay had welcomed guests from Japan, Germany and Australia. Visitors learn to plant paddy, cook rendang and play congkak. Aiman, who is fifteen, helps by guiding guests around the village on bicycles. He says the best part is hearing the guests try to speak Malay. Last month, a German couple sent the family a postcard saying their stay had been the highlight of their trip. The family now plans to build two more rooms.

b.x: JOIN THE YOUNG CODERS CAMP! Ages 13–16. 14–18 December, 9 a.m. – 4 p.m., Science Centre, Shah Alam. Learn to build simple games and apps. No experience needed. Fee: RM120 (lunch included). Bring your own laptop if possible; a few laptops are available to borrow. Register online before 30 November. Places are limited to 40 students.

c.x: On a hot Saturday morning, the Form 3 Geography club took a boardwalk tour through the mangrove forest at Kuala Selangor. Their guide, Encik Faris, explained that mangrove roots trap mud and protect the coast from strong waves. He pointed to tiny fiddler crabs waving one giant claw and to mudskippers that can breathe out of water. In the afternoon, the students planted forty mangrove seedlings along an eroded part of the river bank. Nadia, the club secretary, wrote in her report that the trip had changed how she saw 'muddy swamps'. She now believes that every school should adopt a piece of coastline to protect.

d.x: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to complain about the bicycle I bought from your online store on 2 March. When it arrived on 9 March, a week later than promised, the front brake did not work and the seat was cracked. I have attached three photos. I would like either a full refund or a replacement within fourteen days. I look forward to your prompt reply. Yours faithfully, Lim Wei Jie
